title: The two clock paradox: How short-form content became premium entertainment (and what to do about it)
tldr: Argues entertainment now runs on two clocks — the appointment premiere and the ambient scroll — and brands must design content for both modes of consumption. Directly maps to how people actually consume media today.
angle: Write about designing a content portfolio that serves both 'appointment' and 'ambient' attention.

title: Beauty brand Cakes wants to turn its TikTok virality into an owned media strategy
tldr: Cakes is launching Cakes Media to convert paid TikTok views into a permanent brand-owned audience as ad costs climb. A concrete case study of the shift from rented to owned audiences.
why_fresh: fresh brand case study on owned-media pivot
angle: Break down when virality should convert into an owned-media asset — and the economics behind it.

title: 4 CCO trends communicators should watch
tldr: Hiring execs complain every candidate, newsletter, and interview answer now 'sounds like AI' — pushing human voice back to the top of CCO priorities. Sharp on humanity-over-polish in comms.
why_fresh: new signal on AI sameness in comms hiring
angle: Argue that a distinct human voice is now the scarcest asset in corporate communications.

title: How Shira Lazar grew social account 'What's Trending' to seven figures in revenue
tldr: A creator-led media brand founder's 15-year playbook for building sustainable revenue ahead of the industry curve. Useful creator-economy business-model breakdown.
angle: Extract the durable principles behind creator-led media brands that outlast platform hype.

title: NPR, the quintessential audio news brand, adapts to a video-first future
tldr: NPR lands Casey Newton and Kevin Roose's video-first podcast as it repositions a legacy audio brand for video. A telling case in format migration and brand extension.
angle: How legacy media brands transcreate their identity across formats without losing what made them distinctive.

title: Generative AI is over, in case that wasn't clear
tldr: A provocative take that the naive 'generate five-page reports' era of genAI is ending, and workers should rethink what they actually do. Useful contrarian framing for content teams.
angle: What content work actually looks like once the genAI novelty wears off — from output volume to judgment.

title: This is what women leaders can teach us about using AI well
tldr: Reframes lower female AI adoption not as hesitation but as deliberate, judgment-first use. A human-centered angle on AI habits.
why_fresh: reframes adoption metric as quality signal
angle: Why deliberate, selective AI use beats volume adoption for content quality.

title: Great pitches help reporters understand stories
tldr: With smaller newsrooms and reporters covering unfamiliar beats, PR pros who provide context win. Practical media-relations craft advice.
why_fresh: solid craft advice, not a new trend
angle: Reframe the pitch as an act of teaching, not selling, in a shrinking-newsroom era.

title: The PESO Model Diagnostic: The Novartis Tight End
tldr: Runs Novartis's Super Bowl prostate cancer ad through the PESO model to show what breaks when a single ad has to carry the whole system. Concrete campaign breakdown.
angle: Use the PESO diagnostic to show why one hero asset can't replace an integrated content system.

title: Mark Ritson: The CMO role has shrunk. The extra letters are an attempt to regrow it
tldr: Ritson dissects the proliferation of CxO title variants as a symptom of the shrinking, diluted CMO mandate. Relevant to executive positioning and comms leadership.
why_fresh: new take on eroding executive mandate
angle: What the CMO title inflation says about who really owns the corporate narrative now.

title: AI companies are asking their employees to flag AI writing — and one wants a steak emoji
tldr: Even AI firms are asking staff to mark AI-generated text, revealing internal anxiety about authenticity and human voice. Ties directly to content governance and EGC.
why_fresh: novel governance detail on AI disclosure
angle: Internal AI-disclosure norms as the next frontier of content governance and trust.

title: 5 Signs Your Financial Content Program Has a Credibility Problem
tldr: Argues AI engines and buyers now trust named, credentialed experts, and lists five credibility red flags. Ties author authority to AEO visibility.
angle: Why named human expertise is becoming a hard ranking signal in the AI-answer era.

title: LinkedIn tests advanced creator discovery to power brand campaigns
tldr: LinkedIn is testing tools to help brands find and deploy creators for campaigns, signaling B2B creator-marketing maturation. Relevant platform-strategy shift.
why_fresh: new platform feature for B2B creators
angle: How LinkedIn's creator push reshapes B2B thought-leadership and employee-generated content.

title: Why a laundry brand made four T-shirts you're not supposed to wash
tldr: Ecover and Uncommon made 'lucky' unwashable tees to sell behavior change — a tidy lesson in storytelling for hard-to-shift habits. Nice small-scale campaign case.
angle: Storytelling tactics that sell behavior change instead of features.

title: 50 biggest news websites in UK: Oxford Mail leads audience growth and triples time spent in August
tldr: A local title tripled time-on-site and topped audience growth, an unusual data point on where attention is actually flowing. Useful audience-behavior signal.
angle: What a local paper tripling time-on-site tells us about depth over reach.
